evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks. / Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch) ... Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers (a candidate P3 item; changing it re-tunes every BC fight in the corpus, so it is not a P2 foundation change).

sources_quoted.note: The parsed atom exposes BOTH 8 and 5 as bare percents with no melee/ranged label - i.e. the melee/ranged split survives only in the wiki template, which is exactly the shape of an off-by-one value pick.

sources_quoted.locator: corroboration of the {{rd|melee|ranged}} template convention across 42 uses
sources_quoted.quote: Ravenous Hydra Cleave '{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}'; Titanic Hydra Cleave '{{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}%}} maximum health'; Death's Dance Ignore Pain 'Reduces {{rd|30%|10%}}'; Phage Rage '{{rd|20|10}} bonus movement speed'; Blade of the Ruined King '{{rd|9%|6%}} of the target's current health'
sources_quoted.note: In every case the first parameter is the melee value and the second the ranged value (each matches the live game's melee/ranged split). Therefore Bloodsong's Expose Weakness = 8% for a MELEE holder, 5% for a RANGED holder.

independent_computation.limitation_declared_up_front: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (roster, levels, items, fight length) lives outside the permitted evidence tree - it is not present anywhere under data/ or in docs/math-foundations.md. An absolute re-derivation of 4187.2 from first principles is therefore impossible under the runbook's evidence restriction. What IS derivable from the permitted sources is (a) the authoritative rule values, and (b) a closed-form admissibility envelope that the old and new values can be tested against. Both were done.

step_1_identify_the_only_two_source_mech.black_cleaver_carve: percent armor REDUCTION, 6% per stack, 5 stacks max, 30% cap, 6 s (S2). Per S3 damage scales as 100/(100+R), so more shred => more damage taken.
step_1_identify_the_only_two_source_mech.bloodsong_expose_weakness: flat damage AMPLIFIER on the target, 'from all sources', 4 s, refreshable on a 1.5 s cooldown that starts after the empowered attack; 8% melee / 5% ranged (S1 + S6).

step_2_rule_out_black_cleaver_as_the_mov.argument_a: S4 (read at the same HEAD the leaf values come from) still describes the engine's BC model as the fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant and still lists the Cesaro-mean replacement as an un-taken recommendation. Had this change swapped that model, S4 would have had to be rewritten in the same commit.
step_2_rule_out_black_cleaver_as_the_mov.argument_b: S4 further notes the constant 'changing it re-tunes every BC fight in the corpus' - a BC-model change would move a whole class of golden leaves, not one coupled scenario.
step_2_rule_out_black_cleaver_as_the_mov.argument_c_numeric_envelope: Even the most extreme BC-only story (0.8*5 = 4 stacks -> a hard 5 stacks, i.e. 24% -> 30% shred) needs a specific target armor to land on the observed ratio: (100+0.76A)/(100+0.70A) = 1.0275590 solves at A = 67.7. Any BC-only explanation therefore needs two free parameters (armor and hit count) fitted to one observation; it is unfalsifiable here and is discounted on arguments (a) and (b).

step_3_the_bloodsong_admissibility_envel.model: damage_taken = D * (1 + a * f), where D is the un-amplified damage participant[2] receives, a is the Expose Weakness amplifier, and f in [0,1] is the fraction of that damage that lands inside the 4 s Expose Weakness window.
step_3_the_bloodsong_admissibility_envel.hard_ceiling: For a fixed scenario, swapping a from the ranged 5% to the melee 8% can raise the leaf by at most 1.08/1.05 = 1.0285714, i.e. new <= 4074.9 * 1.0285714 = 4191.33. Any value above that cannot be produced by a source-faithful Expose Weakness model.
step_3_the_bloodsong_admissibility_envel.physical_plausibility_of_f: S1 says Expose Weakness is inflicted BY the empowered basic attack and its 1.5 s cooldown 'starts after using the empowered attack', while the debuff itself lasts 4 s - so after the first proc the debuff has ~100% uptime and only the damage dealt before that first empowered attack lands is un-amplified. A 3.7% un-amplified head (144.4 damage) is exactly the shape that produces, and is the only free parameter the fit needed. Both leaf values fall out of ONE consistent scenario under one free parameter with a physically sensible value.

step_4_direction_test.claim: Under the sourced rule the melee figure is the LARGER one (8% > 5%).
step_4_direction_test.consequence: A correction from the wrongly-applied ranged 5% to the correct melee 8% must RAISE participant[2]'s damage_taken - which is the observed direction. The reverse error (melee -> ranged) would have LOWERED it, and a double-count of the amplifier would have raised it by ~8% (to ~4400), not 2.76%.
step_4_direction_test.old_value_status: 4074.9 is reproduced by the same scenario with a = 5%, i.e. by the RANGED figure. Nothing in the permitted sources makes 5% the right figure for this roster; 5% applies only when the Bloodsong holder is ranged, and the parsed atom (S5) strips the melee/ranged labels, making a wrong pick between the adjacent values 8 and 5 the single most likely defect here.
step_4_direction_test.residual_uncertainty: I cannot read the roster, so I cannot confirm from the permitted evidence that the Bloodsong holder in this scenario is melee. If that holder were ranged, 5% (and therefore the old value) would be right. Weighing against that: the scenario pairs Bloodsong with Black Cleaver (a melee fighter item) in one coupled roster, and the change moves the leaf to the value the melee reading of S1 requires.

independent_computation.conclusion: The new value 4187.2 sits inside the source-attainable envelope for Bloodsong's Expose Weakness, is reproduced exactly by the melee 8% figure quoted in the cached wiki text at a 96.3% debuff coverage that S1's own timing rules make the expected value, and moves in the direction a ranged->melee correction must move. The old value 4074.9 is reproduced only by the ranged 5% figure. Verdict: new_value_correct.

what_would_falsify_this: The Bloodsong holder in cleaver_bloodsong_roster being a RANGED champion (then 5% is right and the old value stood).

The change under test actually being the Black Cleaver Cesaro-mean replacement of docs/math-foundations.md 2.3 (checkable by whether that section was rewritten in the same change, and by whether other cleaver_* leaves moved too).
